doc.title: Albert Murray interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997

title: Thanks to Hamilton, Mr. Sprague and Princeton, closing
summary: Rowe thanks Murray; Murray says Hamilton means much to him because of his inspiring English teacher Mr. Sprague, contrasts Princeton, and the interview ends.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well I wish we could talk all day. But I know you have another engagement to go to. And so it’s really been fascinating, and an honor to have you here on campus. So on behalf of Hamilton College, I’d like to thank you and wish you the best in the future.

Well thank you. You know I feel like a grandson of Hamilton College because my favorite English teacher was from Hamilton. When I was a freshman, the guy that did a lot to inspire me to be a writer, or to embrace the field of literature and to become a writer, was from Hamilton. And I knew about Ezra Pound and people like that at Hamilton. And during that time Alexander Wolcott was a literary voice on radio and all, and he was Hamilton. And so I have always had a consciousness of Hamilton as a place of literary quality and I was especially pleased to get an honorary degree from Hamilton, because of Mr. Sprague, you see? So in a sense personally it is more significant to me than Princeton or something like that. Anyway, they bought into another thing you see? Whereas I bought into all the things I thought they were about. But it turned into something else. Because what I was thinking about was Thomas Mann had a house at Princeton and there was all kinds of guys at Princeton. So I associated with that and Francis Ferguson was writing that fine book on the theater, they had a lot of people. Edmund Wilson was a Princeton guy, and Dean Gauss, Dean Christian Gauss was a great mentor of literary people, but again they were buying in to something else. You know in the Science Department and all that they’re still on the level of Einstein and so forth. But they don’t have any way to look up — they do like the books where they’re looking for a special type thing. What my stuff would do in effect would be to save Princeton, and all that effort, the effort that I thought they represented would be what mine is. Just get the humanities back up front. That’s what I’m about you see? But they want to be politically correct and all of that which is nothing. That’s just crap, you know what I mean? But if you get away from the fundamentals you see each time I start talking about it I want to get to something that’s really basic and very fundamental. Well we certainly appreciate your kind words about the college. It couldn’t come from a more respected writer, and we’re very glad to have you here. All right, thank you very much.
